# word_to_ordinal.word_to_ordinal { #survey_cleaner.word_to_ordinal.word_to_ordinal }

```python
word_to_ordinal.word_to_ordinal(
    data,
    mapping=None,
    likert=None,
    case_insensitive=True,
)
```

Convert a list of text responses to ordinal values
based on a mapping or a pre-defined scale.

This function transforms qualitative string data (e.g., "Very Good") into
quantitative numeric data. It supports custom mappings or built-in standard
scales (Likert scales). It also handles case sensitivity robustness.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Default    |
|------------------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| data             | list of str or pd.Series | A list of string responses to be converted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| mapping          | dict                     | A dictionary mapping text categories (str) to ordinal numbers (int). If None, `likert` must be provided.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `None`     |
| likert           | str                      | The name of a pre-defined likert scale to use. Supported types:  - "agreement": {"Strongly Agree": 5, "Agree": 4, ...} - "satisfaction": {"Very Satisfied": 5, "Satisfied": 4, ...} - "frequency": {"Always": 5, "Often": 4, ...} - "likelihood": {"Very Likely": 5, "Likely": 4, ...}  If None, `mapping` must be provided. | `None`     |
| case_insensitive | bool                     | If True, the conversion will ignore case differences between `data` and the `mapping` keys (e.g., "Good" maps to "good").                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `True`     |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type              | Description               |
|--------|-------------------|---------------------------|
|        | list or pd.Series | Converted ordinal values. |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type       | Description                                                                                                                                  |
|--------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | ValueError | If neither `mapping` nor `likert` is provided, or if both are provided. If a value in `data` acts as a key that is not found in the mapping. |
|        | TypeError  | If input data is not a list or pandas Series.                                                                                                |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Example 1: Using a custom mapping
>>> word_to_ordinal(["Good", "Bad"], mapping={"Good": 1, "Bad": 0})
[1, 0]
```

```python
>>> # Example 2: Using a built-in scale
>>> feedback = ["Strongly Agree", "Agree"]
>>> word_to_ordinal(feedback, likert="agreement")
[5, 4]
```
